title: Persian Saffron Rice with a Golden Crust and Barberries
summary: Saffron-scented basmati rice steams over a buttery, egg-and-yoghurt crust until the top is light and fluffy and the base turns deep golden and crisp, finished with a scattering of glossy barberries.
equipment: 24 cm non-stick pot or deep non-stick frying pan with a lid
wooden spoon with a long handle
large flat serving plate (wider than the pot)

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
ingredients.note: about 1 tsp; for the parboiling water

steps.title: Rinse and soak the rice
steps.text: Rinse the basmati in the bowl, swirling and changing the water 5-6 times until it runs clear, then cover with fresh cold water and leave to soak for 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours. Drain well afterwards. Soaking hydrates the grains evenly so they lengthen and cook through at the same rate once they hit the pot.

steps.title: Steep the saffron
steps.text: Grind the saffron threads to a fine powder in the mortar, then tip it into the small bowl and steep in the 3 tbsp hot water. Crushing the threads first breaks them open so the colour and aroma release fully into the water rather than staying locked inside the strands.

steps.title: Parboil the rice
steps.text: Bring the 2.5 litres of water to a rolling boil with the salt, then add the rice, stir gently and boil for 5-7 minutes. You're looking for grains that have lengthened and are soft on the outside but still have a firm core when you press one between your fingers. Drain in the sieve and rinse under cold water for 30 seconds, which stops the cooking instantly so the rice doesn't turn mushy before it even reaches the pot.

steps.title: Mix the crust layer
steps.text: In a bowl, combine 200g of the parboiled rice with the yoghurt, egg yolk and half the saffron water. The yoghurt and egg yolk set against the hot pan to form the crisp, golden crust, so this mixture needs to be worked through evenly before it goes anywhere near the heat.

steps.title: Line the pot
steps.text: Heat the oil and 30g butter in the non-stick pot over medium heat until the butter foams, then spread the yoghurt rice mixture in an even, pressed layer across the base. Pressing it down firmly now is what gives you a solid, unbroken crust later rather than one that breaks apart on turning out.

steps.title: Mound the remaining rice
steps.text: Spoon the rest of the rice on top, shaping it into a mound that doesn't touch the sides of the pot, then poke 6-8 holes down to the base with the handle of the spoon. These holes give the steam a route up through the mound so every grain cooks evenly rather than just the rice nearest the heat.

steps.title: Sizzle uncovered
steps.text: Cook uncovered over medium-high heat for 8-10 minutes, until you can hear a steady sizzle and see oil bubbling gently at the edges of the pot. This is the point where the base crust starts to form, so resist the urge to cover it too soon.

steps.title: Steam under a wrapped lid
steps.text: Drizzle the butter-water over the mound, then wrap the lid in the tea towel, tying the corners up over the handle and keeping the fabric well away from the flame, and cover the pot tightly. Turn the heat to low and cook for 45-50 minutes, giving the pot a quarter turn every 10-12 minutes so the crust browns evenly rather than just on one side. The towel absorbs the rising steam instead of letting it drip back onto the rice, which is what keeps the top light and fluffy while the base at the bottom turns deep golden; the yoghurt-and-egg crust will comfortably reach well above the 71°C it needs to be fully set.

steps.title: Glaze the barberries
steps.text: Melt the 10g butter in the small frying pan over low heat, add the barberries and sugar and stir for 1 minute until glossy, watching them closely as they burn in seconds. Take them off the heat the moment they look shiny.

steps.title: Rest, then turn out
steps.text: Set the pot on a damp tea towel for 3-4 minutes; the sudden temperature change helps the crust let go of the base. Run a spatula around the edge, place the serving plate over the pot and, holding both firmly with oven gloves, flip the whole thing over in one confident movement before lifting the pot away. Drizzle over the remaining saffron water, scatter with the glazed barberries and cut into wedges so everyone gets a piece of the crust.

tips: Don't shortcut the parboiling: if the grains are too soft before steaming they'll turn mushy, and if too firm the rice won't finish cooking through.
Grind the saffron to a powder before steeping it; crushed threads give far more colour to the golden crust.
Press the yoghurt rice layer down firmly and evenly across the base, since a patchy layer tends to tear when you flip the pot.
Turn the pot a quarter turn regularly during the steaming stage, as a single burner point browns one side of the crust faster than the rest.
Let the pot sit on the damp towel before flipping; skipping this step is the most common reason the crust sticks and breaks apart.
safety: Keep the towel-wrapped lid well clear of the flame at all times, as the fabric can scorch or catch fire.
storage: Cool the rice quickly and refrigerate within 1 hour, then use within 24 hours. Reheat only once, until piping hot and 74°C at the centre; the crust softens on reheating but still keeps its flavour. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
